summary: Humberto Maturana was a philosopher who studied at the University of Chile, University College London, and Harvard University (doctorate, 1956–1958). He was a postdoc at MIT, taught at the University of Chile and UIUC, and founded Instituto Matríztica.

Humphrey William Codrington worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Winchester College and New College (B.A., 1898–1902) before serving in the Ceylon Civil Service from 1903 to 1932.

Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and Harvard University (PhD 1987). He held posts at Harvard and the University of Chicago, as well as visiting positions at NYU and Oxford.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under the doctoral supervision of Mark Allon.

Huston Smith worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Central Methodist University and the University of Chicago (PhD), and under Zuigan Goto, he held posts at Washington University in St. Louis, MIT, Syracuse University, and UC Berkeley.

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the thesis advisement of Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.
Hwansoo Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held a professorship at Duke University (attested 2017) and serves as Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Hyacinth Bitchurin was a sinologist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. Educated at Kazan Theological Academy, he later served as rector of Tobolsk Theological Seminary, worked for the Russian Empire's Foreign Ministry, and was affiliated with the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Hyakudai Sakamoto was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo from 1949 to 1953. He held academic posts at Aoyama Gakuin University, Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences, and The Open University of Japan.

Hyejeong Choi is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held a post as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara in 2015.

Hyla Stuntz Converse was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a B.D. from Union Theological Seminary and a Ph.D. from Columbia University before holding a post at Oklahoma State University in 1974.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Yale University, the University of Freiburg, and Harvard University, and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon from around 1990 to 2004.

Hyoung Seok Ham specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Madhav M. Deshpande, held a postdoc at Kyushu University, and became Assistant Professor at Chonnam National University in 2019.

Hywel David Lewis was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Ysgol Syr Hugh Owen, Bangor University, and Jesus College, Oxford, he later held an academic post at Bangor University from circa 1936 to 1955.

Hélène Brunner-Lachaux was an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied under Jean Filliozat at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held positions at the French Institute of Pondicherry and the National Centre for Scientific Research (1963–1985).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge and serves as Professor and Principle Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

Ian Harris was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge and Lancaster University (doctoral thesis, 1985), he held posts at Lancaster, St Martin's College, St Hugh's College, and the University of Cumbria.

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University in 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University (attested 2005).

Ian Kesarcodi-Watson was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Melbourne, Oxford, McMaster, and Savitribai Phule Pune University (Ph.D., 1982). He held lecturer posts at the University of Hong Kong (1971–1975) and La Trobe University (1975–1984).
